solution: The table is horizontal and smooth, so the particle's weight \(mg\) and the normal reaction from the table are equal and opposite and cancel, and there is no friction. The string tension \(T\) is therefore the ONLY horizontal force acting, and it points along the string towards the peg — that is, towards the centre of the circle. The net force directed towards the centre is thus the tension itself. Newton's second law applied to the circular motion then fixes its size: \(T = \dfrac{mv^2}{l}\). Note that the net force is not zero: the speed is constant but the velocity is continuously changing direction, so the particle is accelerating, and \(\dfrac{mv^2}{l}\) is the magnitude of that centripetal acceleration times the mass — not a separate force to be subtracted from the tension.
